content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Describe the structure of the periodic table
Explain how position relates to properties
is organised in a specific way that reflects the structure of atoms. Understanding its layout helps predict the properties and behaviour of elements.
[DIAGRAM: Periodic table showing groups 1-8/0, periods 1-7, s-block, p-block, d-block labelled, metals and non-metals areas shaded differently]
The periodic table is arranged in:
A vertical column of elements with similar properties.
Elements in the same group have:
Same number of electrons in outer shell
Elements in the same period have:
Properties that change across the period
Transition from metals to non-metals (left to right)
The periodic table is divided into blocks based on which orbital is being filled:
[DIAGRAM: Periodic table with metals on left (shaded), non-metals on right, metalloid staircase in between]
Left and centre of the table
Form negative ions (gain electrons) or covalent bonds
Along the "staircase" dividing metals and non-metals
B, Si, Ge, As, Sb, Te, Po
Have properties of both metals and non-metals
Elements change from metals to non-metals
Reactivity changes (increases for metals, decreases for halogens)
An element is in Group 2 and Period 3. Identify the element and describe its properties.
Explain why elements in the same group have similar chemical properties.
Elements in the same group have the same number of electrons in their outer shell
Chemical reactions involve outer shell electrons
Same number of outer electrons = similar ways of reacting
For example, all Group 1 elements have 1 outer electron
They all lose this electron easily to form +1 ions
This gives them similar chemical properties
Silicon is often described as a metalloid. Explain why.
Silicon is located on the "staircase" between metals and non-metals
Can conduct electricity (when heated or doped)
Its intermediate properties make it a metalloid
It's used as a semiconductor in electronics
Group 0 (noble gases) have FULL outer shells (8, or 2 for He)
Groups are vertical (similar properties); Periods are horizontal (same shells)
Thinking all elements on the left are non-metals
Metals are on the LEFT; non-metals on the RIGHT
Define the terms 'group' and 'period' in the periodic table. (2 marks)
An element has 17 protons. State its group number and period number. (2 marks)
Explain why elements in the same period have the same number of electron shells. (2 marks)
Describe how the properties of elements change across Period 3 from sodium to argon. (4 marks)

Explain the difference between metals and non-metals in terms of their:
   a) Position in the periodic table (1 mark)
   b) Electron behaviour when forming ions (2 marks)
What is a metalloid? Give two examples and explain why they are classified this way. (4 marks)
A vertical column in the periodic table
A horizontal row in the periodic table
A section of the table based on electron orbitals (s, p, d, f)
An element with properties between metals and non-metals
A metal in the d-block of the periodic table
Vertical columns - same outer electrons, similar properties
Horizontal rows - same number of electron shells
Left and centre - lose electrons, form positive ions
Right side - gain electrons or share, form negative ions or covalent bonds
